For a commemoration.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=A commemoratiue {{ls}}acrifice is a true {{ls}}acrifice, no le{{ls}}{{ls}}e then the prefiguratiue {{ls}}acrifices were true {{ls}}acrifices.}}This Sacrifice and Sacrament is to be done perpetually in the Church for the commemoration of Chri{{ls}}t, {{ls}}pecially of his Pa{{ls}}sion: that is to {{ls}}ay, that it may be a liuely repre{{ls}}entation, exemplar, and forme of his Sacrifice vpon the cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e. Of vvhich one oblation on the cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e, not onely al other {{ls}}acrifices of the Lavv vvere figures, but this al{{ls}}o: though this in a more nigh, high, my{{ls}}tical, and maruelous {{ls}}ort then any other. for in them Chri{{ls}}ts death vvas {{ls}}ignified as by re{{ls}}emblance and {{ls}}imilitudes of external creatures and bodies of brute bea{{ls}}ts. but in this of the new Te{{ls}}tament, his body vi{{ls}}ibly {{ls}}acrificed on the cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e, in and by the {{ls}}elf {{ls}}ame body {{ls}}acrificed and immolated in Sacrament and vnder the {{ls}}hapes of bread and wine, is mo{{ls}}t neerely & perfectly re{{ls}}embled: and therfore this is mo{{ls}}t properly commemoratiue, as mo{{ls}}t neerely expre{{ls}}sing the very condition, nature, efficacie, {{ls}}ort, and {{ls}}ub{{ls}}tance of that on the cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e. For which the holy fathers {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ambr. in 10. Hebr. Chry{{ls}}. ho. 17 in ep. ad Hebr''.}}call it the very {{ls}}elf {{ls}}ame {{ls}}acrifice (though in other maner) which was done on the cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e, as it is the {{ls}}elf {{ls}}ame thing, that is offered in the Sacrament, and on the cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e. Whereby you may {{ls}}ee the peruer{{ls}}itie of the Prote{{ls}}tants or their ignorance, that thinke it therfore not to be Chri{{ls}}ts body, becau{{ls}}e it is a memorie of his body or a figure of his body vpon the cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e: nor to be a true {{ls}}acrifice, becau{{ls}}e it is a commemoratiue {{ls}}acrifice. for as the thing that more liuely, neerely, and truely re{{ls}}embleth or repre{{ls}}enteth, is a better figure then that which {{ls}}hadoweth it a far of: {{ls}}o this his body in the Sacrament, is more perfectly a figure of Chri{{ls}}ts body & {{ls}}acrifice, then any other. Chri{{ls}}t him {{ls}}elf the Sonne of God is a figure and character of his fathers per{{ls}}on, being yet of the {{ls}}elf {{ls}}ame {{ls}}ub{{ls}}tance. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=To be a figure of a thing, and yet the thing it {{ls}}elf, repugneth not.}}and Chri{{ls}}ts body transfigured on the holy Mount, was a figure and re{{ls}}emblance of his per{{ls}}on glorified in heauen. euen {{ls}}o is his body in the Sacrament to a faithful man that knoweth by his beleefe grounded on Chri{{ls}}ts owne vvord, that in the one forme is his body, in the other his bloud, the mo{{ls}}t perfect repre{{ls}}entation of his death that can be. As for the {{ls}}acrifice, it is no le{{ls}}{{ls}}e a true Sacrifice, becau{{ls}}e it is commemoratiue of Chri{{ls}}ts Pa{{ls}}sion: then tho{{ls}}e of the old Te{{ls}}tament were the le{{ls}}{{ls}}e true, becau{{ls}}e they vvere prefiguratiue. for that is the condition annexed to al Sacrifice of euery Lavv, to repre{{ls}}ent Chri{{ls}}ts Pa{{ls}}sion.

''20. The nevv Te{{ls}}tament in my bloud.''] Moy{{ls}}es tooke the bloud of the fir{{ls}}t {{ls}}acrifice that vvas made after the geuing of the Lavv ''Exod. 24''. and vvith bloud confirmed the couenant and compact betvvixt God and his people, and {{ls}}o dedicated the ''old Te{{ls}}tament'', vvhich without bloud ({{ls}}aith S, Paul) {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Hebr. 9''.}}vvas not dedicated. Moy{{ls}}es put that bloud al{{ls}}o into a {{ls}}tanding peece, and {{ls}}prinkled al the people &c. vvith the {{ls}}ame, & {{ls}}aid the{{ls}}e formal vvordes, ''This is the bloud of the couenant'' &c. or (as it is read in S. Paul) {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''ver{{ls}}. 20''.}}''of the Te{{ls}}tament which God hath deliuered vnto you''. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Both te{{ls}}taments dedicated in bloud.}}Vnto al which, Chri{{ls}}t in this action about the {{ls}}econd part of this his {{ls}}acrifice, in euery of the Euangeli{{ls}}ts mo{{ls}}t cleerely alludeth, expre{{ls}}sing that the ''new Te{{ls}}tament'' is begonne and dedicated in his bloud in the Chalice, no le{{ls}}{{ls}}e then the old vvas dedicated, begonne, and ratified in that bloud of calues conteined in the goblet of Moy{{ls}}es. vvith vvhich his ovvne bloud he {{ls}}prinkled invvardly his Apo{{ls}}tles as the fir{{ls}}t fruits of the new Te{{ls}}tament, imitating the wordes of Moy{{ls}}es, and {{ls}}aying, ''This is the Chalice the new Te{{ls}}tameut &c'': Which the other Euangeli{{ls}}ts {{ls}}pake more plainly, ''This is my bloud of the new Te{{ls}}tament''. By al which it is mo{{ls}}t certaine, that Chri{{ls}}tes bloud in the Chalice, is the bloud of Sacrifice, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The external religion of the new Te{{ls}}tament principally in the {{ls}}acrifice of the altar.}}and that in this {{ls}}acrifice of the altar con{{ls}}i{{ls}}teth the external religion and proper {{ls}}eruice of the new Te{{ls}}tament, no le{{ls}}{{ls}}e then the {{ls}}oueraine wor{{ls}}hip of God in the old Law did con{{ls}}i{{ls}}t in the {{ls}}acrifices of the {{ls}}ame. For though Chri{{ls}}tes {{ls}}acrifice on the Cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e and his bloud {{ls}}hed for vs there, be the general price, redemption, and {{ls}}atisfaction for vs all, and is the la{{ls}}t and perfecte{{ls}}t {{ls}}ealing or confirmation of the new law and Te{{ls}}tament: yet the {{ls}}eruice and Sacrifice which the people of the new Te{{ls}}tament might re{{ls}}ort vnto, could not be that violent action of the Cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e, but this on the Altar, which by Chri{{ls}}tes owne appointment is and {{ls}}hal be the eternal office of the new Te{{ls}}tament, and the continual application of al the benefites of his Pa{{ls}}sion vnto vs.

''20. Which {{ls}}hal be {{ls}}hed.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''The chalice {{ls}}hed for vs'', mu{{ls}}t needes {{ls}}ignifie, the bloud therein, not vvine, and the {{ls}}ame {{ls}}acrificed.}}{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''calix qui the chalice which τὸ ποτήριον τὸ ἐκχυνόμενον''}}It is much to be ob{{ls}}erued that the relatiue, ''which'', in the{{ls}}e vvordes is not gouerned or ruled (as {{ls}}ome vvould perhaps thinke) of the nowne ''bloud'', but of the word ''chalice''. Which is mo{{ls}}t plaine by the Greeke. Which taketh away al cauillations and {{ls}}hifts from the Prote{{ls}}tants, both again{{ls}}t the real pre{{ls}}ence and the true Sacrificing. For it {{ls}}heweth euidently, that the bloud as the contents of the chalice, or as in the chalice, is {{ls}}hed for vs (for {{ls}}o the Greeke readeth in the pre{{ls}}ent ten{{ls}}e) and not onely as vpon the cro{{ls}}{{ls}}e. And therfore as it foloweth thereof inuincibly, that it is no bare figure, but his bloud in deede, {{ls}}o it en{{ls}}ueth nece{{ls}}sarily, that it is a Sacrifice, and propitiatorie, becau{{ls}}e the chalice (that is the Bloud contained in the {{ls}}ame) is {{ls}}hed for our {{ls}}innes. For al that know the maner of the Scriptures {{ls}}peaches, know al{{ls}}o that this, ''Bloud to be {{ls}}hed for {{ls}}inne'', is to be {{ls}}acrificed for propitiation or for pardon of {{ls}}innes. And this text proueth al this {{ls}}o plainely, that {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Beza condemneth the Go{{ls}}pel it {{ls}}elf of fal{{ls}}hod and impo{{ls}}sibilitie.}}{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=* ''Annot. no. Te{{ls}}t. 1556''.}}Beza turneth him {{ls}}elf roundly vpon the Holy Euangeli{{ls}}t, charging him with Solœci{{ls}}me or fal{{ls}}e Greeke, or els that the wordes (which yet he confe{{ls}}seth to be in al copies Greeke and Latin) are thru{{ls}}t into the text out of {{ls}}ome other place: which he rather {{ls}}tandeth vpon then that S. Luke {{ls}}hould {{ls}}peake incongruou{{ls}}ly in {{ls}}o plaine a matter. And therfore he {{ls}}aith plainely that it can not be truely {{ls}}aid neither of the chalice it {{ls}}elf nor of the contents thereof: vvhich is in deede to giue the lie to the ble{{ls}}sed Euangeli{{ls}}t, or to deny this to be Scripture.
